title: Proper-endomorphism units commute with open and closed compact-support composition
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and separated finite-type $k$-schemes of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with ordinary finite-coefficient operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Let $t:X\to X$, $t_U:U\to U$ and $t_Z:Z\to Z$ be proper $k$-endomorphisms with $tj=jt_U$, $ti=it_Z$, and suppose the square for $j$ is Cartesian. For $h=j,i$, put $W=U,Z$, respectively, and let
$$b_{t,j}:Lt^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!Lt_U^*,\qquad b_{t,i}:Lt^*Ri_*\to Ri_*Lt_Z^*$$
be respectively the canonical open exchange and the closed-square adjunction mate. No Cartesian hypothesis on the closed square is imposed. Identify $Ri_!=Ri_*$ by proper coincidence. Write $H_V=R\Gamma_c(V,-)$ and $a_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for $V=X,U,Z$. For each $r=t,t_U,t_Z$, let
$$\beta_{r,N}:H_V(N)\longrightarrow H_V(Lr^*N)$$
be induced by $N\to Rr_*Lr^*N$, the canonical proper comparison $Rr_*=Rr_!$, compact-support composition, and $a_Vr=a_V$. Let $\lambda_{h,N}:H_X(Rh_!N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_W(N)$ be the canonical compact-support composition isomorphism. Then for every $N\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$,
$$\lambda_{h,Lt_W^*N}\circ H_X(b_{t,h,N})\circ\beta_{t,Rh_!N}=\beta_{t_W,N}\circ\lambda_{h,N}.$$
All terms are read on the bounded constructible finite-Tor domains of the operations. The same equality holds for their filtered lifts on bounded-below finite filtrations whenever the underlying and graded inputs lie in those domains. Here the filtered lifts are those of [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts].

proof.text: Work at the fixed finite ring $A$. Every bounded constructible pro-etale input has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), and the operations below preserve the bounded-below etale-origin class. Thus the compactification-independent composition isomorphisms of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and the normalization statement [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization], apply to every object occurring below. All arguments stay on these bounded-below domains; the bounded constructible finite-Tor conditions are imposed only where the statement imposes them. No etale/pro-etale transport of units or mates is used: every identity below is stated and used for the pro-etale operations.

source.place: Step 6, final paragraph; domains of the composition law

proof.text:
For $h:W\to X$ write $J_h=Rh_!$, $P=Lt^*$, $R=Rt_*$, $Q=Lt_W^*$ and $S=Rt_{W*}$. Proper coincidence and compact-support composition [prop-functor-package](3), [thm-sf-comp-composition] give the canonical comparison
$$\chi_h:J_hS\xrightarrow{\sim}R J_h$$
by $Rh_!Rt_{W!}\simeq R(ht_W)_!=R(th)_!\simeq Rt_!Rh_!$, with $Rt_{W!}=Rt_{W*}$ and $Rt_!=Rt_*$ the proper-coincidence comparisons of the compactifications $(\mathrm{id},t_W)$, $(\mathrm{id},t)$. This is the map $\chi$ of [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization] for the square $ht_W=th$ (with $h'=h$, $W'=W$, $X'=X$). For $h=i$, clause (1) of that lemma says that, with $Ri_!=Ri_*$, $\chi_i$ is the ordinary direct-image composition comparison $Ri_*Rt_{Z*}\simeq R(it_Z)_*=R(ti)_*\simeq Rt_*Ri_*$ in the normalization of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3). For $h=j$ the open square is Cartesian, and clause (2) says that $\chi_j$ is the adjunct under $j_!\dashv j^*$ of $\lambda^{-1}$, where $\lambda:j^*Rt_*j_!\to Rt_{U*}j^*j_!\simeq Rt_{U*}$ is the open exchange followed by the inverse open unit. No inverse to a closed-square base-change map is used.

For the open piece put $J=j_!$, $K=j^*$, with open unit $u:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}KJ$ and counit $e:JK\to\mathrm{id}$ [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]; $J$ is fully faithful, so a map $JM\to N$ is determined by its transpose $M\to KN$. Let $c:KP\xrightarrow{\sim}QK$ be the pullback comparison for $tj=jt_U$ [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), and let $\mathrm{Ex}:KR\to SK$ be the mate of $c^{-1}:QK\to KP$ under $P\dashv R$, $Q\dashv S$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; thus $\lambda=S(u^{-1})\circ\mathrm{Ex}_J$. The open exchange $b:PJ\xrightarrow{\sim}JQ$ of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] restricts on $U$ to the identity after these identifications: $K(b_N)=u_{QN}\circ Q(u_N^{-1})\circ c_{JN}$. Hence $K(b^{-1}_N)\circ u_{QN}=c^{-1}_{JN}\circ Q(u_N)$. By [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility], the transformation $JQ\to PJ$ whose mate under $J\dashv K$, $J\dashv K$ is $c^{-1}$ has the same transposes; so $b^{-1}$ is that inverse mate. Apply [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] twice. (a) To $J\dashv K$, $J\dashv K$ (horizontal), $Q\dashv S$, $P\dashv R$ (vertical) and $\alpha=b^{-1}:JQ\to PJ$: the iterated mate $\mathrm{Ex}$ is the conjugate of $b^{-1}$ for $PJ\dashv KR$, $JQ\dashv SK$. (b) To $Q\dashv S$, $P\dashv R$ (horizontal), $J\dashv K$, $J\dashv K$ (vertical) and $\alpha=b$: if $\beta_b:JS\to RJ$ is the mate of $b$ under $Q\dashv S$, $P\dashv R$, then the mate of $\beta_b$ under $J\dashv K$ is the conjugate of $b$. Conjugation reverses composition and preserves identities [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], so this conjugate is $\mathrm{Ex}^{-1}$ (in particular $\mathrm{Ex}$ is invertible). By [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] for this $J$-mate, the transpose of $\beta_b$ is $K(\beta_{b,N})\circ u_{SN}=\mathrm{Ex}^{-1}_{JN}\circ S(u_N)=\lambda^{-1}_N$. By Step 2 the transpose of $\chi_j$ is also $\lambda^{-1}$, so $\chi_j=\beta_b$:
$$\chi_{j,N}=R(J\varepsilon_{Q,N})\circ R(b_{SN})\circ\eta_{P,JSN},$$
with $\varepsilon_Q:QS\to\mathrm{id}$. This identifies the specified map, not an arbitrary isomorphism $JS\simeq RJ$.

source.place: Step 6, final paragraph; explicit adjunction-mate calculation below

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] to this mate pair, with $L_1=Q$, $R_1=S$, $L_2=P$, $R_2=R$, and both vertical functors equal to $J$. It gives
$$\chi_{j,QN}\circ J(\eta_{Q,N})=R(b_N)\circ\eta_{P,JN}.$$
Thus the unit on the open localization piece, followed by its open exchange, is the unit on $U$, followed by the canonical proper/open composition comparison. This is a direct specialization of the cited unit equation.

source.place: Step 6, final paragraph; explicit adjunction-mate calculation below

proof.text:
For the closed piece put $I=Ri_*$, $K=Li^*$, with unit $u:\mathrm{id}\to IK$ and counit $v:KI\to\mathrm{id}$ [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Let $a:KP\xrightarrow{\sim}QK$ be the pullback comparison for $ti=it_Z$. By the definition of a square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate],
$$b_{t,i,N}=I(Qv_N)\circ I(a_{IN})\circ u_{PIN}.$$
Let $d:RI\xrightarrow{\sim}IS$ be ordinary direct-image composition; thus $d=\chi_i^{-1}$. The composite-unit formula [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), or equivalently [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the unit normalization [lem-trf-adjoint-mate](2), gives, for every $M$,
$$IS(a_M)\circ d_{KPM}\circ R(u_{PM})\circ\eta_{P,M}=I(\eta_{Q,KM})\circ u_M.$$
Both sides are the unit of the adjunction for $it_Z=ti$, written using $KP$ and $QK$. This uses commutativity only. In particular the closed square is not asserted to be Cartesian.

source.place: Step 6, final paragraph; explicit adjunction-mate calculation below

proof.text:
Substitute $M=IN$ in the last equation and postcompose with $IS(Qv_N)$. Naturality of $d$ and the formula for $b_{t,i,N}$ turn the left side into $d_{QN}\circ R(b_{t,i,N})\circ\eta_{P,IN}$. Naturality of $\eta_Q$ turns the right side into
$$I(\eta_{Q,N})\circ I(v_N)\circ u_{IN}=I(\eta_{Q,N}),$$
the last equality being the triangle identity for $K\dashv I$. Cancel $d_{QN}=\chi_{i,QN}^{-1}$ to obtain
$$R(b_{t,i,N})\circ\eta_{P,IN}=\chi_{i,QN}\circ I(\eta_{Q,N}).$$
No stalk argument, nilpotent invariance, or invertibility of $b_{t,i}$ enters this calculation.

source.place: Step 6, final paragraph; explicit adjunction-mate calculation below

proof.text:
For either $h$, Steps 4 and 6 give $R(b_{t,h,N})\eta_{t,J_hN}=\chi_{h,QN}J_h(\eta_{t_W,N})$. Apply $H_X$ and insert the proper-composition maps $c_{r,M}:H_V(Rr_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_V(M)$ used to define $\beta_r$. By naturality,
$$H_X(b)\,\beta_{t,J_hN}=c_{t,J_hQN}\,H_X(Rb\,\eta_{t,J_hN}).$$
Associativity of compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition], with proper coincidence as in [prop-functor-package](3), says
$$\lambda_{h,QN}\,c_{t,J_hQN}\,H_X(\chi_{h,QN})=c_{t_W,QN}\,\lambda_{h,SQN}.$$
Indeed both sides compose the three direct-image factors for $a_Xht_W=a_Xth=a_Wt_W=a_W$, using the definition of $\chi_h$ in Step 2. Finally naturality of $\lambda_h$ at $\eta_{t_W,N}$ gives
$$\lambda_{h,QN}H_X(b)\beta_{t,J_hN}=c_{t_W,QN}H_W(\eta_{t_W,N})\lambda_{h,N}=\beta_{t_W,N}\lambda_{h,N},$$
which is the asserted equation.

source.place: Step 6, final paragraph; explicit adjunction-mate calculation below

proof.text: Repeat the argument in the bounded-below filtered derived categories with finite filtrations. [lem-trf-filtered-derived-operation-lifts] supplies the adjunctions with their units and counits, the square mates, the open comparison, the proper comparisons and the compact-support composition/refinement comparisons, and says that lifting respects composition and whiskering. The equalities of Steps 2–3 are equalities of ordinary transformations built from these units, counits, square mates and comparisons; since the lifts respect composition and whiskering, they hold for the lifts, and the iterated-mate identity [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] holds for the lifted adjunctions as well. The unit equation of Step 4 and the composite-unit/triangle calculation of Steps 5–6 are identities in any category with these adjunctions, so they hold before applying either the forgetful or graded functors. The naturality and associativity calculation of Step 7 therefore gives the required equality of filtered morphisms. Forgetting or taking a graded piece recovers the unfiltered equation by the stated comparison maps. This does not infer equality of filtered morphisms from equality of their underlying or graded maps. The required bounds and operation domains are precisely those imposed on the underlying and graded inputs in the statement.
